introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information and Communication Technologies (0796), Paper 3 (practical), June 2022. Duration: two hours. Answer ALL tasks.**

The booklet reproduced here contains two versions of the same practical paper, headed Group 1 and Group 2: they have the same two tasks (Task A: spreadsheet; Task B: programming) with a few differences in wording, and a different algorithm in Task B.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is required to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

The working file (the SALES workbook) is supplied on the day in the Candidate folder; it is not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP 2 - TASK A (SPREADSHEET: 18 MARKS)**

Open the SALES workbook in the candidate folder. This workbook contains three worksheets, Sales, OldSales and Summary. *[Workbook supplied on the day, not reproduced here.]*

Questions 1 to 9 are based on the **Sales** sheet.
incertitudes: Le PDF contient DEUX versions de la même épreuve pratique : « Group 1 » (pages 1 à 3) et « Group 2 » (pages 4 à 6). Les deux sont transcrites, en quatre exercices : G1-A et G1-B (Group 1), G2-A et G2-B (Group 2) ; `groupes` vaut ["GROUP 1"] ou ["GROUP 2"] (même convention que l'ICT 2020 Paper 3). Différences : en Task A, la question 10 (remplissage bleu des noms de champs des feuilles OldSales et Summary) est imprimée dans le Group 1 mais ABSENTE du Group 2 (voir plus bas) ; en Task B, l'algorithme du Group 1 calcule un prix total (U, Q, T = U*Q, test U=11 et Q=7), celui du Group 2 calcule un effectif total (N1, N2, TS = N2+N1, test N1=53 et N2=15) et la question 1 n'est pas la même (objectif de l'algorithme / une instruction d'entrée et une de traitement). Le reste de la Task A est identique mot pour mot.

Les fichiers de travail du jour de l'examen (classeur SALES avec les feuilles Sales, OldSales et Summary) ne figurent pas dans le PDF. La disposition des colonnes de la feuille Sales (A SN, B NAME, C 3% Discount, D Unit Price, E Quantity, F Payable Total, G Item) est DÉDUITE des références de cellules du sujet (C4, F12, C25, plages A1:G25 et D2:G25) et du même sujet de 2020 ; le contenu et la disposition de OldSales et de Summary sont inconnus : les formules des questions 12 et 13 (`=OldSales!B6`, `VLOOKUP`, `SUMIF` avec les plages A2:A30 et C2:C30) reposent sur une disposition supposée (OldSales : Item en A, Unit Price en B, Quantity en C ; Summary : noms d'articles en B), dite comme telle dans le corrigé. Les lignes de données 2 à 24 de la feuille Sales sont supposées d'après le cadre A1:G25 et la ligne de totaux 25.

Aucun tableur n'a été exécuté : les formules de tableur n'ont pas été testées dans un tableur. Seuls l'exemple illustratif (prix 900, quantité 11 : remise 297, à payer 9 603), la somme conditionnelle (tableau OldSales fictif de 5 lignes : 20 + 15 + 10 = 45 pour Spanner), le tri alphabétique et la largeur 19 x 7 + 5 = 138 pixels ont été recalculés avec Python. La conversion de 138 pixels en 19 caractères vaut pour Excel avec la police par défaut (Calibri 11) : valeur déduite d'un calcul, non testée. Les valeurs d'exemple (900 et 11) ne viennent pas de ce sujet : elles sont illustratives et dites telles dans le corrigé.

Aucun compilateur C ni Pascal n'est disponible : les programmes C (ANSI C) et Pascal (ISO) du corrigé de la Task B n'ont PAS été compilés. Leur logique a été vérifiée par une traduction fidèle en Python, exécutée sur les données de test du sujet ; les sorties recopiées dans le corrigé (« Total price = 77.00 » pour le Group 1 avec U=11 et Q=7 ; « Total number of students = 68 » pour le Group 2 avec N1=53 et N2=15) sont celles de cette simulation. L'en-tête `program Calculator(input, output);` est la forme stricte de l'ISO 7185 ; l'affichage `T:1:2` est une largeur minimale positive (la largeur 0 n'est pas acceptée par tous les compilateurs).

Défaut d'impression, Group 1, Task B : l'en-tête imprime « PROGRAMMING: 17 marks » alors que les points des questions s'additionnent à 19 (2 + 2 + 2 + 10 + 3) ; le Group 2 imprime « 19 Marks » avec les mêmes points. Les points ne sont pas corrigés : 17 est repris tel qu'imprimé dans `points` de G1-B, 19 dans G2-B.

Défaut d'impression, Group 2, Task A : la question 10 manque (la page 2 s'arrête à la question 9, la page 3 commence à la question 11 ; la phrase « The next exercises are based on the OldSales and Summary sheets » du Group 1 manque aussi). Les points imprimés des questions présentes totalisent 17 (1+2+1+2+2+1+1+2+1+1+1+2) alors que l'en-tête imprime 18 : le point manquant correspond vraisemblablement à la question 10 du Group 1 (1 mark), mais la question n'est pas inventée : le fichier G2-A saute de la question 9 à la question 11. Group 1, Task A : l'en-tête imprime 18 et les points des 13 questions totalisent bien 18 (1+2+1+2+2+1+1+2+1+1+1+1+2).

Défauts d'impression, Task B : le sujet imprime DEUX lignes de réponse (« Variable 1 », « Variable 2 ») pour identifier les variables, alors que chaque algorithme utilise TROIS variables (U, Q, T pour le Group 1 ; N1, N2, TS pour le Group 2) : le corrigé donne les trois et accepte deux d'entre elles. Dans les pieds de page des pages 2 et 3 du Group 1, le code est imprimé « 2022/0790/3/G1 » au lieu de 0796 (page de garde : 0796). La consigne de la page de garde imprime « is require » (recopié tel quel). La question 11 de la Task A dit « Sort the table in OldSales by items » sans préciser l'ordre (le Group 1 et le Group 2 sont identiques ; l'ordre croissant est supposé, comme dans le sujet 2020).

Les barèmes détaillés (« Marking ») des corrigés sont des propositions : le sujet n'imprime que les points par question. Les zones de réponse du livret (lignes à compléter pour les formules, les variables et les types, le résultat final) ne sont pas reproduites en figure : elles sont signalées dans les énoncés. Aucune figure n'a été recadrée : le sujet ne contient ni schéma ni tableau de données. Les filigranes de gcerevision.com, les cadres d'en-tête (numéro de centre, nom du candidat, cadre « For examiners' use only ») et les artefacts de scanner sont ignorés.

questions.enonce_markdown: Change the font type of the first row (showing SN, NAME, 3% Discount ...) to ALGERIAN. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the whole first row (click the row heading **1**, or select the header cells A1:G1), then on the **Home** tab open the *Font* box and choose **Algerian** (or Format Cells > Font > Font). Only the font *type* changes: the size, the text and the other cells stay as they are. If Algerian is not listed, it is not installed on that computer and the supervisor is told.

*Marking:* 1 mark if every header cell of row 1 (SN, NAME, 3% Discount, ...) is in Algerian.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert cell border in the range A1:G25. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the range **A1:G25** (click A1, then Shift + click G25; or type A1:G25 in the Name Box). On the **Home** tab open the *Borders* menu and choose **All Borders** (or Format Cells > Border > *Outline* and *Inside*, then OK). The outline AND the inner grid lines must both appear, so that every cell of the range has a border on its four sides.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the outside border, 1 mark for the inside borders.

questions.enonce_markdown: Adjust the Name field width to 138 pixels. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Right-click the heading of the Name column (column B) and choose **Column Width...** (or Home > Format > Column Width). In Excel with the default font (Calibri 11) one character is 7 pixels wide and each column adds 5 pixels of padding, so 138 pixels = 19 x 7 + 5 corresponds to a width of **19** characters: the dialog box then shows *19.00 (138 pixels)*. The same value appears in the pop-up when the column boundary is dragged with the mouse.

*Marking:* 1 mark for a Name column whose width is 138 pixels.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Insert a formula in the *3% Discount* field to calculate the discount for each item bought.

This discount is 3% of the product of Unit Price and Quantity.

Write down the formula in cell C4. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The discount is 3% of (Unit Price x Quantity). In the sheet the 3% Discount field is column **C**, the Payable Total is column **F** (both are named in the question) and the numeric fields Unit Price and Quantity are in columns **D** and **E** (the printed paper does not show the sheet: this layout is deduced from the cell references of questions 4 to 6, from the range of question 9 and from the order requested in question 8). The formula is typed in the first data cell and copied down the column (fill handle), so the row number changes automatically:

```
C4: =0.03*D4*E4
```

Equivalent forms are accepted: `=3%*D4*E4`, `=D4*E4*0.03`, `=(D4*E4)*3/100`. The formula must start with `=`, use cell references (not typed numbers such as 297), and the multiplication sign `*` (not x). Illustrative check (values chosen for the example, not taken from the paper): for a unit price of 900 and a quantity of 11, the product is 9,900 and the discount is 9,900 x 0.03 = 297.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the 3% factor, 1 mark for the product of Unit Price and Quantity with correct references.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Insert a formula in the *Payable Total* field to calculate the total price for each sale. The total is calculated following the algorithm below

```
Start
    Multiply Unit Price by Quantity to get total price
    Subtract the 3% Discount from the total price above
Stop.
```

Write down the formula in to calculate the Payable Total in F12 in the line below. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The algorithm has two steps: (1) total price = Unit Price x Quantity, (2) Payable Total = total price - 3% Discount, where the discount has already been calculated in column C (question 4). In row 12:

```
F12: =D12*E12-C12
```

The formula is then copied down the whole column. A formula that recomputes the discount, `=D12*E12-0.03*D12*E12` or `=D12*E12*(1-3%)`, gives the same value and is also accepted, but the first form follows the algorithm exactly (it reuses the 3% Discount cell). Illustrative check with the example of question 4: 900 x 11 = 9,900; 9,900 - 297 = **9,603**.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the product Unit Price x Quantity, 1 mark for the subtraction of the discount.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the total of *3% Discount* and total of the *Payable Total* in row 25.

Write down the formula in cell C25. *[1 mark]*

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The totals are obtained with the `SUM` function over the data rows of each column (header in row 1, data from row 2 to row 24, totals in row 25). The question asks for the cell **C25**, which lies under the 3% Discount column:

```
C25: =SUM(C2:C24)
```

The total of the Payable Total is calculated in the same way under its own column: `F25: =SUM(F2:F24)`. A selection of the two columns followed by the *AutoSum* button (Home > AutoSum, or Alt + =) writes both formulas at once. The data rows 2 to 24 are deduced from the borders of question 2 (range A1:G25 with the totals in row 25); if the data stopped before row 24 the range would be shortened accordingly.

*Marking:* 1 mark for `=SUM(C2:C24)` (or an equivalent range of the same column).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Set the font of row 25 to bold and size 14. *[1 mark]*

*Ensure that you have written down the formulae in the cells in questions 4, 5 and 6 above before attempting the questions that follow.*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click the heading of row **25** to select the whole row, then on the **Home** tab press **Bold** (Ctrl + B) and set the font size box to **14**.

*Marking:* 1 mark if row 25 is both bold and in size 14. (The reminder printed under the question asks the candidate to copy the formulae of questions 4 to 6 into the booklet before the columns are rearranged in question 8 and the formulae move.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Rearrange the fields (columns) in this sheet to occur in the order SN, Name, Item, Unit Price, Quantity, 3% Discount and Payable Total. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The columns are in the order SN (A), Name (B), 3% Discount (C), Unit Price (D), Quantity (E), Payable Total (F), Item (G) (order deduced from the cell references of the paper). The requested order is SN, Name, **Item**, Unit Price, Quantity, **3% Discount**, Payable Total. Two moves are enough, using *Cut* and *Insert Cut Cells* (not Copy, so that the formulae keep working and their references are updated):

1. Select column **G** (Item), Cut (Ctrl + X), right-click the heading of column **C** and choose **Insert Cut Cells**: the order becomes SN, Name, Item, 3% Discount, Unit Price, Quantity, Payable Total.
2. Select column **D** (3% Discount), Cut, right-click the heading of column **G** (Payable Total) and choose **Insert Cut Cells**: the order becomes SN, Name, Item, Unit Price, Quantity, **3% Discount**, Payable Total.

Final layout: A SN, B Name, C Item, D Unit Price, E Quantity, F 3% Discount, G Payable Total. The formulae follow their cells: the discount is now `=0.03*D2*E2` in F2, the payable total `=D2*E2-F2` in G2, and the totals of row 25 become `=SUM(F2:F24)` in F25 and `=SUM(G2:G24)` in G25. (Dragging a column with the Shift key held down gives the same result.)

*Marking:* 1 mark for the Item column placed third, 1 mark for the remaining columns in the requested order.

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the numbers in the range D2:G25 to thousand separator without decimal place. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the rearrangement of question 8, the range **D2:G25** holds Unit Price (D), Quantity (E), 3% Discount (F) and Payable Total (G); the Item column (C) is text and is not included. Select the range, open **Format Cells** (Ctrl + 1) > **Number** tab > category *Number*, set *Decimal places* to **0** and tick **Use 1000 Separator (,)**. (The *Comma Style* button followed by two clicks on *Decrease Decimal* gives the same display.) A value such as 9603 is displayed 9,603 and a discount of 181.5 is displayed 182 (rounded for display only): the stored values are unchanged.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the thousand separator with 0 decimal places on the whole range.

questions.enonce_markdown: Sort the table in **OldSales** by items. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click inside the table of the **OldSales** sheet (or select the whole table, headers included), then **Data > Sort**, tick *My data has headers*, choose the **Items** column in *Sort by* and the order **A to Z** (the order is not stated in the question; ascending is the usual one). The whole table must be sorted, not only the Items column, so that every row keeps its own unit price and quantity. If OldSales repeats an item on several rows, those rows are grouped together. The sort comes BEFORE the links of questions 12 and 13, because a link points to a cell address, not to an item.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the table sorted by Items, with the rows intact.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In C2 in the **Summary** sheet, type a formula to link C2 to a cell in **OldSales** that contains the unit price of spanners. Do similarly for the cells in the range C3:C9. *[1 mark]*

Write down the formula in cell C5 in the line below.

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A link is a formula made of an equals sign followed by a reference to a cell of another sheet: `=SheetName!CellAddress`. Each cell of column C of the Summary sheet is linked to the cell of the sorted OldSales table that contains the unit price of the item listed on the same row of Summary. The OldSales sheet is not printed, so its layout is assumed here: Item in column A, Unit Price in column B, Quantity in column C, the first item on row 2. The simplest way to write the link is to type `=` in the Summary cell, click the sheet tab OldSales, click the cell holding the price, and press Enter. For example, if after the sort of question 11 the unit price of spanners is in cell B9 of OldSales:

```
C2: =OldSales!B9
```

The cell asked, **C5**, is linked in the same way to the unit price of the item listed on row 5 of the Summary sheet; its address depends on where that item stands in the sorted OldSales table, for example:

```
C5: =OldSales!B6
```

if that item is on row 6 of OldSales (the number 6 is only an example). Because the link is a plain reference, the Summary cell shows the price held in OldSales and follows any change made there. A lookup formula such as `=VLOOKUP(B5,OldSales!$A$2:$B$30,2,FALSE)` (item name in B5 of Summary) is an alternative that does not depend on the row position, but the question asks for a direct link to a cell.

*Marking:* 1 mark for a formula of the form `=OldSales!<cell>` pointing to a unit price (and the others filled in the same way in C3:C9).

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the **Summary** sheet, type a formula in D2 that will add the total quantity of spanners sold as declared in **OldSales**. Do similarly for the cells in the range D3:D9. Write down the formula in cell D2 in the line below. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*

**Print the three sheets of this workbook: Sales, OldSales and Summary.**
questions.corrige_markdown:
The quantity sold of an item is the sum of the Quantity values of all the OldSales rows whose Item is that item: this is a conditional sum, `SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range)`. With the layout assumed in question 12 (OldSales: Item in A, Unit Price in B, Quantity in C, data from row 2 to row 30) and the name of the item written in cell B2 of the Summary sheet:

```
D2: =SUMIF(OldSales!$A$2:$A$30,B2,OldSales!$C$2:$C$30)
```

The ranges are absolute (`$A$2:$A$30`, `$C$2:$C$30`) so that they stay fixed when the formula is copied down to D3:D9, while the criterion `B2` is relative and becomes B3, B4, ... B9, giving one total per item. The version with the name typed inside the formula, `=SUMIF(OldSales!$A$2:$A$30,"Spanner",OldSales!$C$2:$C$30)`, gives the total for spanners too but would have to be edited for every row. For instance, if OldSales held three spanner rows of 20, 15 and 10 units (illustrative values), D2 would show 45 (checked with a small script).

Finally the three sheets (Sales, OldSales and Summary) are printed (File > Print > *Print Entire Workbook*, or each sheet in turn) and inserted in the booklet.

*Marking:* 1 mark for `SUMIF` (or `SUMPRODUCT`) with the item as criterion and the correct range of items, 1 mark for the correct sum range (the Quantity column), the ranges being anchored so that the formula can be copied down.
